value.rationale: N=2 is the sharp loss-of-stationarity boundary for a natural globally reset Brownian gas. Its physically needed replacement is a nonstationary joint law: synchronized random logarithmic exponents, universal distance ratio, explicit all-positive joint moments, and subunit limiting Pearson correlation π/4. These quantify an unresolved physical regime rather than a numerical parameter tweak. The log-age input itself is correctly credited to classical renewal theory.
